chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: The believer has only one 'awrah (private part).
And in the ritual bath (ghusl), there are three.

key_terms.عَوْرَةٌ: Private part or area of the body that must be covered

ai.seo_question: What are the differences in covering requirements between prayer and ritual bath in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) distinction between the *'awrah* in prayer (one part) and during *ghusl* (three parts), reflecting the juristic principle that the requirement for covering is context-dependent. This hadith underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding modesty, distinguishing between the static posture of prayer and the dynamic movements of ritual purification.
